content.text: Compiles cleanly. Before removing the dpct helpers, I need to check whether `scan_input.hpp` also pulls them in.

The only remaining dpct dependency is in the generated `scan.dp.cpp`; `scan_input.hpp` is already plain C++. Next I'll rewrite the file with plain SYCL 2020: `sycl::queue`, `malloc_device`/`free`, `nd_range<1>`, and `local_accessor`. I'm also adding one barrier at the end of each grid-stride iteration so the shared buffer isn't overwritten by the next block while another work-item is still reading the previous result.

input.summary: Ported scan.cu to plain SYCL 2020 in migrated/scan.dp.cpp (scan_input.hpp unchanged, already plain C++). Changes from the SYCLomatic output: removed all dpct:: helpers, DPCT macros and #include <dpct/...>; the queue is sycl::queue (in-order), memory uses sycl::malloc_device/sycl::free, the launch is a 1-D sycl::nd_range<1> with 16*max_compute_units groups of N/2=256 work-items, shared memory is sycl::local_accessor<T,1> passed as a raw pointer, and barriers are sycl::group_barrier(item.get_group()). I also added one group barrier at the end of each grid-stride iteration in both kernels, so a work-group's next block doesn't overwrite shared temp while other work-items are still reading the previous result (the original CUDA has the same hazard). Both kernels and the Blelloch algorithm are otherwise unchanged. The file compiles with icpx -fsycl with add_dpct_include=false and zero diagnostics. Not verified: I had no tool to execute build/candidate, so the exact-match check of both integer outputs against the C++ reference (within atol=0, rtol=0) has not been run.
